hook.line: Mariana asks Tomás how good his Spanish is. A flat *Hablo español* would sound like bragging, so he does what every Spanish speaker does: he softens it.

examples.en: I don't know anything about football.
Do you know Medellín well? (to a friend)
I know the city a little.

rule:
Spanish speakers hedge by default. A bare *Hablo francés* can sound like a big claim, so you add how much:
*nada*: nothing
*un poco*: a little
*bastante bien*: quite well
*muy bien*: very well

Before a noun, *un poco* takes *de*: *un poco de francés*. Next to the verb on its own, no *de*: *Conozco un poco la ciudad*.

*Nada* needs *no* in front of the verb: *No sé nada de fútbol*.

In Colombia you'll hear *un poquito* all the time: a tiny bit.
smallPrint: Teachers call these hedges. *Saber de* means to know about a subject: *Hernando sabe mucho de carros*.

options: I don't know Bogotá at all.
I know a bit about football.
I don't know anything about football.
I know the city very well.
I know the city a little.
Hernando knows a little about cars.
Hernando doesn't know anything about cars.
Hernando knows a lot about cars.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Hablo ___ de francés.* (*un poco* or *bastante bien*) I speak a little French.
yourTurn.why: A little is *un poco*, and before a noun it takes *de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No sé ___ de fútbol.* (*nada* or *un poco*) I don't know anything about football.

yourTurn.why: A place you know is *conozco*, and quite well is *bastante bien*.

accept: Vale habla muy bien el inglés.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Do you know Medellín well?
yourTurn.why: *Conoces* for a friend and a place, plus *bien*.

yourTurn.prompt: Soften it to a little: *Hablo francés.*
yourTurn.why: Add *un poco de* before the language.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it nothing at all: *Sé un poco de fútbol.*
yourTurn.why: *Nada* after the verb needs *no* in front of it.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Before a noun, *un poco* needs *de*.
With *nada* after the verb, Spanish also puts *no* in front.
How you do something is *bien*, not *bueno*.

personal: Rate yourself honestly in two lines: one thing you know *un poco* and one you know *bastante bien*. Your Spanish counts.
